usage:
Usage: nscb split <source> [bundle-directory] [--replace | --skip] [--json | --jsonl]

Write one selected regular file as numbered Split parts in a bundle directory. Without a destination, NSCB uses <source-name>.split inside the configured output_dir or Documents/NSCB_output. The bundle contains a canonical <source-name> directory and an adjacent <source-name>.nscb-split.json manifest. Give resolve the canonical directory or one numbered member. The default policy refuses a different existing bundle. An exact qualified match is reported as already up to date; --replace does not replace a different existing bundle, and --skip leaves the destination unchanged. The production part size is fixed. Destination filesystems must meet the current local APFS qualification. For accepted work, --json emits one job.result document and --jsonl emits ordered job.event records followed by one job.result document. Invocation and planning errors before job admission emit a kind:error document.
created: Split bundle published at {bundle}. Resolve the canonical directory at {canonical}. Manifest: {manifest}.
already_up_to_date: Split bundle already matches the planned source: {bundle}.
skipped: Split left the existing bundle unchanged: {bundle}.
cancelled: Split was cancelled before the receipt commit.
internal_failure: Split ended without an authoritative result.
unknown_error: Split ended in an unrecognized state.
cleanup_warning: Operation-owned recovery data was retained because cleanup could not be proven safe.
